headline: DepthWizard turns a single 2D image into an interactive 3D flythrough
summary: This project uses monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation to reconstruct a 3D mesh, enabling virtual camera movement through the scene. It aims to provide rapid 3D spatial data without specialized hardware.
details: DepthWizard converts a single 2D image into an interactive 3D flythrough. This project addresses the challenge of acquiring real elevation data, which typically requires expensive and slow methods like LiDAR or photogrammetry, especially crucial for rapid terrain surveys or disaster response.

The system processes an image through monocular depth estimation to generate a dense depth map. It then applies semantic segmentation to identify ground features like buildings and trees, reconstructing them into a 3D mesh for camera navigation.

Under the hood, DepthWizard leverages a robust stack including Depth Anything V2 for depth, SAM 2/SegFormer for segmentation, and Open3D/PyVista for mesh reconstruction. CesiumJS handles the geospatial scene rendering, all powered by a React frontend and Python/FastAPI backend.

A key learning was that monocular depth models provide relative depth, not trusted elevation. Achieving georeferenced, usable data required significant calibration, scale estimation, and tying outputs to DEM/GCP reference points, a process not readily available from pretrained models.

The project was a submission for the Smart India Hackathon, competing against 160 teams. Despite its technical ambition and use of open-source tools, the team did not advance past the internal round, highlighting the challenge of explaining complex projects in limited time.

The developer plans to evolve DepthWizard from a hackathon prototype into a complete, working model by the end of the semester/year, with a full video walkthrough to be shared then. The current output includes screenshots of the depth/heat map generation.
